purpose: Deep source research for Basra (WUP 5262) after the 2026-10-08 overnight pass ended with official_registry_geometry_not_public.
name: Basra

priorStatus.finding: Basra Real Estate Registration Directorate (Ministry of Justice) and the municipal building-permit procedure (title deed Form 25 plus a boundary map) are evidenced; no anonymous parcel geometry. The Az Zubayr (5290) and Al Qurna (5233) records in the same governorate reached the same result.

summary: No public parcel polygon source for Basra was found in English or Arabic searches. The registry is held by the Ministry of Justice, which offers per-parcel deed and map requests only, and only in six Baghdad directorates (May 2025). Basra's governorate and municipal sites have no GIS. The governorate's old interactive map was a WordPress page of Google Maps points and is now suspended. The nearest public vector data is UN-Habitat's Basra master-plan land-use layer on ArcGIS Online. It is browser-readable (CORS *) but holds land-use blocks of 1 to 50 ha, not parcels. Residential plots in Basra are about 200 m².

nearestPublicLayerNotParcels.operator: UN-Habitat Regional Office for Arab States (ArcGIS Online org unhabitat-roas), Basrah Urban Portal
nearestPublicLayerNotParcels.browserAccess: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on query; reachable from the laptop (ArcGIS Online, global).
nearestPublicLayerNotParcels.vintage: Item created 2021-04-26, data last edited 2021-06-01; BMP_LU suggests the Basra Development Strategy and Master Plan land-use base.
nearestPublicLayerNotParcels.whyNotParcels: Each polygon is a land-use block (EX/PR Horizontal Residential, Open Space, Canals, Road and so on) keyed by planning district (C16, B07 and so on). Residential blocks in the central sample are 0.24 to 52 ha (median about 6 ha), whereas the UN-Habitat Basra Urban Profile gives an average plot of 200 m². A block can hold hundreds of plots.

measurements.result: 195 polygons in 11 planning districts (C16 76, C13 37, C12 17 ...); OBJECTID unique in sample, ET_ID 184 distinct; median 0.89 ha across all classes; the 41 residential blocks run from 0.24 to 52.2 ha

otherRoutes.source: Ministry of Justice e-services (deed and property map), https://www.moj.gov.iq/view.9289/
otherRoutes.finding: On 22 May 2025 the ministry launched per-parcel e-deed and property-map requests (طلب سند وخارطة للعقار) in six Baghdad directorates (Kadhimiya 1, Sadr 2, Rusafa 2, Bayaa, Shaab, Karkh 1). It is a request form, not a map viewer. No Basra rollout was found.
otherRoutes.access: Request per parcel, not usable as a source.

otherRoutes.source: Basra Real Estate Registration Directorate, https://www.moj.gov.iq/view.8135/
otherRoutes.finding: Confirms the registry custodian. No public map, no GIS endpoint.

Wayback capture (2021-04-14) is a WordPress page with Google Maps API markers for commercial, leisure, sport and government points and a login. It has no parcels and no GIS service. The host now redirects to a suspended-account page.

otherRoutes.source: Basra Municipalities Directorate https://baladyatbasrah.gov.iq/ and Basra Municipality https://basrabaladya.gov.iq/ (permits portal https://lbm.basrabaladya.gov.iq/)
otherRoutes.finding: Both are reachable (200). They are news and e-service sites (building permits, revenue, plot-registration notices) with no map or GIS links. The permit portal needs an application number.

otherRoutes.source: Iraqi government GIS hostnames (gis.basra.gov.iq, gis.basrah.gov.iq, geoportal.basra.gov.iq, basrah.gov.iq, mocmhm.gov.iq, dgcs.gov.iq, survey.gov.iq, gisportal.mop.gov.iq, geoportal.mop.gov.iq, rerd.moj.gov.iq)
otherRoutes.finding: None resolve in DNS from the laptop, so they are not geo-fenced live hosts. mowr.gov.iq redirects to a secure-gateway error page. boc.oil.gov.iq (Basra Oil Company) returns a JavaScript verify wall.
The deed and map services sit behind a citizen login. There is no anonymous geometry.

otherRoutes.source: ArcGIS Online search (basra, basrah, البصرة, مقاطعة, قطعة, قطع, عقار, اراضي, ملكية, parcel/cadastral/plots with Iraq and Basra terms, zubair, umm qasr, rumaila, basra master plan, basra zoning)
otherRoutes.finding: No parcel layer. Hits were UN-Habitat land use and master plan (above), informal-settlement points and honeycomb grids, city and sub-district boundaries, thematic POIs, 145 survey points, and Rumaila oil field and UXO clearance boundaries. Four public web maps (owners GIS_3D_EXPERT and aida.shmais) hold a CAD-derived zoning set of 52 zone polygons of 0.8 to 20 km². The Safwan_IRAQ_gdb service needs a token. The UN-Habitat ROAS HLP housing-plot layers are in Ninewa (about 42E 36N), not Basra.
Zero datasets for basra. The Iraq datasets are boundaries, settlements, HOT OSM buildings, GHSL and urban profiles of Duhok, Erbil and Sulaymaniyah. None has parcels.

otherRoutes.source: GitHub repository search (basra cadastral, basra/basrah parcels, iraq cadastre, iraq parcels shapefile)
Academic literature (University of Basrah theses, IASJ, FIG)
otherRoutes.finding: Land-use and urban-expansion studies (for example Abu al-Khasib 2014, Basra 1977-2016 residential change, Landsat 4D maps) do not publish parcel data. FIG 'Examination of Land Registration System in Iraq' says registration runs through about 18 MOJ offices, records are on paper, and boundary drawings have no common coordinate system, so they cannot be used as cadastral maps.

otherRoutes.source: Donor programmes: UN-Habitat MULK (EU-funded land-records digitisation), UN-Habitat Basra Urban Profile (2020), JICA Basrah water-supply GIS, Basra Development Strategy and Master Plan (Directorate General of Physical Planning, MGP consortium)
otherRoutes.finding: MULK pilots and training centres are in Baghdad and Erbil, built on STDM, and publish nothing. The Urban Profile PDF has no data annex for cadastral or GIS data. The JICA GIS has only boundary, district, road and water layers. The master-plan land use is the UN-Habitat layer above.
Has landuse and building polygons but no parcels. A count query against overpass-api.de failed (empty response) and was not retried.

sideFindings: UN-Habitat ROAS (services7.arcgis.com/S9LAFnsxHsSpUJFQ) also publishes Basra informal-settlement points and honeycomb layers and an Iraq-wide Informal_settlements polygon layer. All are CORS-open, and none are parcels.
Atlas GIS Iraq (owner salallaq, services1.arcgis.com/lUwoyaNpSIRMtnlf) hosts nationwide thematic Iraq layers (districts, schools, heritage, ports, elections). It has no cadastral layer.
Iraqi cadastral identity is the muqata'a (مقاطعة, district number with a name) plus the qit'a (قطعة, plot number). No public source carrying those keys was found for Basra.
openQuestions: Whether the MOJ deed-and-map e-service will reach the Basra and Zubayr directorates. If it does, it is still a per-parcel request and not a map layer.

Whether the UN-Habitat MULK digitisation or the Basra Directorate of Urban Planning holds digitised muqata'a sheets that could be released on request. That would need direct contact; no public channel was found.
Licence of the UN-Habitat land-use layer, if it is ever wanted as a context or zoning overlay.
nextStep: Keep Basra held with no runtime adapter. Re-check only if the MOJ e-service or MULK publishes map data for Basra, or through a direct data request to the Basra Real Estate Registration Directorate or UN-Habitat Iraq. The UN-Habitat land-use layer must not be imported as parcels.
